summary: Concrete-block lookout with steel cab on Inyo NF, built 1963 after a 1943 original; out of full-time service in the 1980s, volunteer-staffed again since 2024.

facts.design: Current building: 16 by 40 ft concrete block lookout with a 10 by 10 ft steel cab, built 1963; original 1943 structure built by the Civilian Public Service

access.note: Forest road open 24 hours a day with no fee. The cab is a working lookout staffed by volunteers, and the sources read give no visitor rule for it, so check with the Mono Lake Ranger District before climbing up.

visit.trail_note: Logging Camp Road from Highway 395 at Deadman Summit, then Forest Service route 1S05 to the lookout. High-clearance 4x4 recommended.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Inyo National Forest (Mono Lake Ranger District)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the original lookout structure was built in 1943 and the current 16 by 40 ft block lookout in 1963; FFLA says it was built in 1963. Both are kept: 1943 for the original, 1963 for the current building.
NHLR lists the cooperator as the Mono Lakes Ranger District, while FFLA and the Forest Service use Mono Lake Ranger District. The correct name is Mono Lake Ranger District.

notes_for_editor: Do not confuse with us-ca-bald-mountain-sierra-nf (a different lookout in Sierra NF). The record's '2024 assessed' event (site visit on 24 May) is not in any page read, so it is left out. The record's access value 'unknown' is replaced with public, based on the Forest Service road page and the FFLA visitor count. The 1956 and 1969 items come from newspaper quotes reproduced on the weebly page, not from the newspapers themselves. The FFLA testimonials on the host page are dated September 2026, which hints at 2026 staffing, but no 2026 report was read, so staffing is dated 2025. The 1980s end of full-time service has no exact year in the sources, so it has no dated event. The PDF calls the lookout '61-year-old'; that is not used.
